sentences.text: The FIR in question was lodged initially as a missing person report alleging that the applicant had enticed away the daughter of the informant.
Subsequently, in the statement under section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she had gone out of her own free will and also stated that both had married together.
In the statement under section 164 Cr.P.C. also, she did not support the prosecution story.
In the ossification test, the age of victim is prima-facie determined as 19 years.

5. Considering the statements under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. being contrary to the version as contained in the FIR and the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 27.02.2023, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
Thus the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Lokesh Gurjar be released on bail in aforesaid first information report number subject to his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of Rs.25000/- (Twenty Five Thousand) each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
